stories.author: Dave Bryce
stories.published: 2012 (page URL dated 29 Nov 2012; no date shown on the page)
stories.summary: Cycles about 12 miles each way from Bolton to work at HMRC in Salford, usually two days out of a four-day week. He says it takes as long as the bus.

stories.author: Laura (first name only)
stories.destination_text: Office near Old Street, London (via Cannon Street)
stories.mode: Walk, Southeastern train to Cannon Street, walk
stories.duration: Just under two hours each way
stories.summary: Walks about half an hour to Tonbridge station, takes a 45-minute train (station to station) to Cannon Street, then walks about 25 minutes. Works from home a couple of days a week.
stories.note: Old Street sits on the Islington–Hackney boundary, so this story isn't linked to one destination area.

stories.author: Paul (first name only)
stories.destination_text: Office near Charing Cross, London (via Waterloo)
stories.mode: Train to Waterloo, walk across Hungerford Bridge
stories.summary: Takes the train from Surbiton to Waterloo and walks across Hungerford Bridge to an office near Charing Cross. About an hour door to door most days, more when things go wrong.

stories.author: Morgan (first name only)
stories.mode: Lift to the station, TfL Rail, Underground, London Northwestern train, then bus, taxi or walk
stories.duration: Two hours at best; plans for two and a half
stories.summary: A dance teacher who travels from Romford to work in Tring three times a week, crossing London via Liverpool Street and Euston.

stories.author: Rachel Amery (named in The Scotsman's accompanying video)
stories.mode: Train (7am service with 14 stops via Fife)
stories.summary: A political journalist's commute from Perth to Holyrood: about 45 miles. She notes the faster direct line via Kinross closed in 1970.
